title: Normalized coefficient calculus for extension and reduction stages
statement: Fix a finite field datum D, a prime l different from its characteristic, a finite extension E/Q_l, separated finite-type schemes T,X,Z over Spec(D.k), a separated finite-type map f:T->X over that base, a closed immersion i:Z->X over the base, and a compactification c of X->Spec(D.k). For the actual stage system and canonical maps of [def-sf-finite-free-coefficient-comparison-data], there exist an ordinary-etale Calculus et and a pro-etale Calculus pro satisfying Normalized. On every stage arrow a, pro.closedMap a on every finite-Tor constructible input is exactly proClosedMap of a.ringMap, and pro.omegaMap a is exactly proOmegaMap. No ramification, finite-free arithmetic conclusion or scheme-isomorphism square is asserted by this lemma.

source.place: Paragraphs 1--3, construction of the five canonical comparisons, evaluation/double dual, extension/reduction coherence and site transport; excludes scheme-isomorphism naturality and arithmetic conclusions.

proof.text: Factor a stage arrow into an equal-exponent finite extension followed by reduction in the upper field. The valuation ring extension is finite free; reducing its basis proves finite freeness of the first factor. The ramification identity identifies base-parameter ideals with powers of the upper uniformizer.

On the finite-free factor apply the exact derived scalar calculus and the direct/compact image comparison. Transpose the inverse closed image comparison and counit, and apply the exceptional-mate theorem. The finite-free Hom calculation identifies the evaluation transpose as an isomorphism. On the quotient factor use the finite coefficient direct-image, closed-shriek, dualizing and Hom theorems. The Verdier arrow is their Hom/dualizing composite. Preserve finite-Tor constructibility and reflect ordinary closed equations from bounded etale origin. To reconcile the published coefficient universes, choose a small algebraically isomorphic model of the finite-dimensional coefficient field. The valuation and integer quotient ring identifications induce equivalences of module sheaves and derived categories, preserving balanced tensor, evaluation and counit maps. Transfer the ULift quotient statements through these equivalences.

Choose the descended normalized balanced tensorator and Koszul symmetry. Transpose the same evaluation/counit to verify evaluation, double-dual and naturality identities. Refine two arrow factorizations to an extension/reduction grid. Horizontal transitivity, vertical quotient cocycles and the mixed ramified square prove all five composition identities with the specified scalar associator; identity maps give the units.

Use the finite-duality site comparison and finite-free site transport for the five squares. The site unit/counit identify the transported closed and dualizing arrows with the explicit proClosedMap and proOmegaMap. Full faithfulness on the bounded etale-origin domain reflects equalities. Assemble these fields into the two Calculus structures and Normalized.

theorem normalized_stage_coefficient_calculus
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type (u + 1)) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (T X Z : Scheme.{u})
    [T.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Z.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (T ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (T ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (T ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (Z ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Z ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Z ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (f : T ⟶ X) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [i.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))]
    (c : Compactification (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))) :
    ∃ (et : Sites.Calculus false l E f i c) (pro : Sites.Calculus true l E f i c),
      Sites.Normalized l E f i c et pro ∧
      (∀ {s t : Stage l E} (a : Arrow s t) (M : Sites.D true s.ring X),
        Sites.Ctf true s.ring X M → pro.closedMap a M = Sites.proClosedMap a.ringMap i M) ∧
      (∀ {s t : Stage l E} (a : Arrow s t),
        pro.omegaMap a = Sites.proOmegaMap a.ringMap c)
